questions.accessible_text:
1. [Maximum mark: 6]

In a group of 20 girls, 13 take history and 8 take economics. Three girls take both history and economics, as shown in the following Venn diagram. The values p and q represent numbers of girls.

[Diagram: A rectangle labelled U contains two overlapping circles labelled history and economics. The history-only region is labelled p, the intersection is labelled 3, and the region outside both circles is labelled q.]

(a) Find the value of
    (i) p;
    (ii) q. [4]

(b) A girl is selected at random. Find the probability that she takes economics but not history. [2]
questions.summary: Complete a two-set Venn diagram and find a probability.
questions.solution: History only is p = 13 − 3 = 10. Economics only is 8 − 3 = 5, so q = 20 − (10 + 3 + 5) = 2. Therefore the probability of economics but not history is 5/20 = 1/4.

questions.accessible_text:
2. [Maximum mark: 5]

Let f(x) = 5x and g(x) = x² + 1, for x ∈ ℝ.

(a) Find f⁻¹(x). [2]

(b) Find (f ∘ g)(7). [3]
questions.summary: Find a linear inverse and evaluate a composite function.
questions.solution: From y = 5x, interchange x and y: x = 5y, hence f⁻¹(x) = x/5. Also g(7) = 7² + 1 = 50, so (f ∘ g)(7) = f(50) = 250.

questions.accessible_text:
3. [Maximum mark: 6]

The following diagram shows triangle PQR.

[Diagram not to scale: Triangle PQR has ∠PQR = 30°, ∠QRP = 45°, and side PQ = 13 cm.]

∠PQR = 30°, ∠QRP = 45° and PQ = 13 cm.

Find PR.
questions.summary: Use the sine rule to find a side of a triangle.
questions.solution: PR is opposite 30° and PQ = 13 is opposite 45°. By the sine rule, PR/sin30° = 13/sin45°, so PR = 13(1/2)/(√2/2) = 13/√2 = 13√2/2 cm.

questions.accessible_text:
4. [Maximum mark: 6]

Jim heated a liquid until it boiled. He measured the temperature of the liquid as it cooled. The following table shows its temperature, d degrees Celsius, t minutes after it boiled.

[Table: t (min): 0, 4, 8, 12, 16, 20; d (°C): 105, 98.4, 85.4, 74.8, 68.7, 62.1.]

(a) (i) Write down the independent variable.
    (ii) Write down the boiling temperature of the liquid. [2]

Jim believes that the relationship between d and t can be modelled by a linear regression equation.

(b) Jim describes the correlation as very strong. Circle the value below which best represents the correlation coefficient.

0.992    0.251    0    −0.251    −0.992 [2]

(c) Jim’s model is d = −2.24t + 105, for 0 ≤ t ≤ 20. Use his model to predict the decrease in temperature for any 2 minute interval. [2]
questions.summary: Interpret cooling data, correlation and a linear model.
questions.solution: The independent variable is t (time), and the boiling temperature is d = 105°C at t = 0. The data decrease very strongly, so the best coefficient is −0.992. The model changes by −2.24(2) = −4.48°C in two minutes, so the predicted decrease is 4.48°C.

questions.accessible_text:
5. [Maximum mark: 7]

(a) Find ∫ x e^(x²−1) dx. [4]

(b) Find f(x), given that f′(x) = x e^(x²−1) and f(−1) = 3. [3]
questions.summary: Integrate an exponential by substitution and use an initial condition.
questions.solution: Let u = x² − 1, so du = 2x dx. Then ∫x e^(x²−1)dx = (1/2)∫eᵘdu = (1/2)e^(x²−1) + C. Hence f(x) = (1/2)e^(x²−1) + C. Since f(−1) = 1/2 + C = 3, C = 5/2, and f(x) = (1/2)e^(x²−1) + 5/2.

questions.accessible_text:
6. [Maximum mark: 6]

The following diagram shows the graph of f′, the derivative of f.

[Diagram: Coordinate axes with x shown from approximately −4 to 10 and y from approximately −12 to 8. A smooth curve y = f′ has a local minimum at A near (1.5, −5), then rises through the labelled point (4, −2), reaches a local maximum at B at approximately (6, 0), and then decreases.]

The graph of f′ has a local minimum at A, a local maximum at B and passes through (4, −2).

(a) The point P(4, 3) lies on the graph of the function f.
    (i) Write down the gradient of the curve of f at P.
    (ii) Find the equation of the normal to the curve of f at P. [4]

(b) Determine the concavity of the graph of f when 4 < x < 5 and justify your answer. [2]
questions.summary: Read gradient and concavity information from a derivative graph.
questions.solution: At x = 4, f′(4) = −2, so the gradient is −2. The normal gradient is −1/(−2) = 1/2; through P(4,3), y − 3 = (1/2)(x − 4), or y = x/2 + 1. For 4 < x < 5 the graph of f′ is increasing, so f″ > 0 and f is concave up.

questions.accessible_text:
7. [Maximum mark: 8]

The first three terms of a geometric sequence are ln(x¹⁶), ln(x⁸), ln(x⁴), for x > 0.

(a) Find the common ratio. [3]

(b) Solve ∑_(k=1)^∞ 2^(5−k) ln x = 64. [5]
questions.summary: Use logarithm laws and sum an infinite geometric series.
questions.solution: Using ln(xⁿ) = n ln x, the terms are 16lnx, 8lnx, 4lnx, so r = 1/2. In part (b), the first term (k=1) is 2⁴lnx = 16lnx and the ratio is 1/2. Thus the sum is 16lnx/(1−1/2) = 32lnx. Therefore 32lnx = 64, ln x = 2, and x = e².

questions.accessible_text:
8. [Maximum mark: 17]

A line L₁ passes through the points A(0, 1, 8) and B(3, 5, 2).

(a) (i) Find vector AB.
    (ii) Hence, write down a vector equation for L₁. [4]

(b) A second line L₂ has equation r = (1, 13, −14) + s(p, 0, 1). Given that L₁ and L₂ are perpendicular, show that p = 2. [3]

(c) The lines L₁ and L₂ intersect at C(9, 13, z). Find z. [5]

(d) (i) Find a unit vector in the direction of L₂.
    (ii) Hence or otherwise, find one point on L₂ which is √5 units from C. [5]
questions.summary: Work with intersecting perpendicular lines in three dimensions.
questions.solution: (a) AB = (3,4,−6), so L₁ may be written r = (0,1,8) + t(3,4,−6). (b) Perpendicular direction vectors have zero dot product: (3,4,−6)·(p,0,1) = 3p−6 = 0, hence p = 2. (c) The x-coordinate on L₁ gives 3t=9, so t=3; then z=8−6(3)=−10 (and y=1+4(3)=13). (d) The direction (2,0,1) has magnitude √5, so a unit vector is (1/√5)(2,0,1). Moving √5 from C gives C ± (2,0,1), hence for example (11,13,−9) (or (7,13,−11)).

questions.accessible_text:
9. [Maximum mark: 14]

A quadratic function f can be written in the form f(x) = a(x − p)(x − 3). The graph of f has axis of symmetry x = 2.5 and y-intercept at (0, −6).

(a) Find the value of p. [3]

(b) Find the value of a. [3]

(c) The line y = kx − 5 is a tangent to the curve of f. Find the values of k. [8]
questions.summary: Determine a quadratic and find slopes of tangent lines by discriminant.
questions.solution: The roots are p and 3, whose midpoint is 2.5, so (p+3)/2=2.5 and p=2. Since f(0)=a(−2)(−3)=6a=−6, a=−1. Thus f(x)=−(x−2)(x−3)=−x²+5x−6. Intersections with y=kx−5 satisfy −x²+5x−6=kx−5, or x²+(k−5)x+1=0. Tangency requires discriminant zero: (k−5)²−4=0, so k−5=±2 and k=3 or 7.

10. [Maximum mark: 15]

The following table shows the probability distribution of a discrete random variable A, in terms of an angle θ.

[Table: a: 1, 2; P(A = a): cos θ, 2 cos 2θ.]

(a) Show that cos θ = 3/4. [6]

(b) Given that tan θ > 0, find tan θ. [3]

(c) Let y = 1/cos x, for 0 < x < π/2. The graph of y between x = θ and x = π/4 is rotated 360° about the x-axis. Find the volume of the solid formed. [6]
questions.summary: Use a probability distribution, trigonometric identities and a volume of revolution.
questions.solution: (a) Probabilities sum to 1, so cosθ + 2cos2θ = 1. With cos2θ = 2cos²θ−1 and c=cosθ, 4c²+c−3=0=(4c−3)(c+1). Since cosθ is a probability, c≥0, so cosθ=3/4. (b) sinθ=√(1−9/16)=√7/4; tanθ>0 selects the positive value, tanθ=√7/3. (c) V=π∫_θ^(π/4)sec²x dx=π[tanx]_θ^(π/4)=π(1−√7/3).
